Issued at 242 PM CDT Thu Sep 24 2026

An area of steady light to locally moderate rainfall 
extends from around a Slayton to Yankton line and points east. 
This area of rain will gradually push east through the remainder
of the afternoon and start to fall apart this evening over 
northwest Iowa. However, patchy drizzle will be possible after 
this rain departs especially along and east of I-29. A bit drier
in the low-levels over parts of northwest Iowa tonight, so it
may take a bit longer for drizzle to develop there. Farther 
west, especially into south-central South Dakota, we will see 
some breaks in the clouds which will allow temperatures to warm 
into the middle 70s. Some instability (around 500-750 J/kg) will
be present along and ahead of a weak front over south-central 
South Dakota where this heating is occurring, but plenty of dry
mid-level air should prevent scattered showers and storms from
developing in these locations. In the off chance (<10%) we get a
storm, severe weather is not expected as weak effective shear
looks to be place.

Heading into tonight, a few showers will continue to be possible 
mainly along the Highway 20 corridor. Low stratus looks to spread 
back west through the night, but before it spreads back into south-
central South Dakota, patchy fog can't be ruled out there. Drizzle 
will begin to become more likely heading into early tomorrow morning 
as cloud ceilings continue to fall, so keep the rain gear handy for 
your Friday morning commute. Scattered light showers will develop 
throughout the day, with chances gradually lifting northward through 
the afternoon due to strengthening warm air advection at 850 mb. 
These will be more of the hit or miss variety unlike what we 
saw today, so keep that umbrella nearby but rain totals will 
only be a few hundredths to a tenth of an inch during the day on
Friday, except for locally higher amounts along the Highway 20 
corridor Friday morning. Lowered the high temperatures a bit 
from the NBM for Friday given the cloud cover and drizzle, with 
highs mostly in the lower 60s. If some peaks of sun can be 
realized, a few middle to upper 60s for highs will be possible.


Rain chances will increase Friday night into Saturday morning as the 
main upper wave pivots through the area. The highest rainfall totals 
during this time frame will generally be over northwest Iowa and 
adjacent areas of southeast South Dakota and far northeast Nebraska, 
where around a half an inch to an inch of rain can be expected. A 
few pockets of 1-1.5" of rain (15-25% chance) can't be ruled out 
mainly along and southeast of a Spencer to Sioux City line. This 
rain should be spread out long enough where flash flooding concerns 
will be low where these highest amounts occur, but still be prepared 
for wet roads if traveling especially early Saturday morning. 

Showers and very isolated storms will gradually push east through 
the afternoon, though once again some patchy drizzle will remain 
possible after any of the rain showers end at least through the 
early evening Saturday. Drizzle details will be refined as we 
get closer to the Saturday afternoon. Though some very patchy 
drizzle will be possible into Sunday morning, should mostly see 
dry weather for the day. This should allow for some of the 
warmest temperatures that we've see over the past few days, with
highs in the upper 60s to middle 70s. Ultimately, these 
temperatures will be dependent on how quickly we can scatter out
any morning clouds, so expect changes to the forecasted 
temperatures as we approach Sunday. 

Rain chances do look to return once again on Monday, but especially 
Monday night into Tuesday. This will be as the West Coast longwave 
trough finally swings into the area. Will have to watch for any 
heavy rain once again with this activity, especially on top of the 
rainfall we've seen the past week. LREF probabilities show around a 
30-40% chance of at least an inch of rainfall Monday night through 
Tuesday night, focused over northwestern Iowa. Trends will continue 
to be monitored as we get closer to next week.
